title: 5 Animal Superpowers That Sound Fake
hook: These five animal superpowers sound fake. Number one shouldn't be possible.

countdown.narration: At number five, the archerfish. Imagine picking one familiar face out of a wall of photographs. Researchers trained this fish to recognize a human face, even when tested against forty-four unfamiliar faces.

At number four, the peacock mantis shrimp. You might expect something this small to be slow. Instead, its strike reaches twenty-three meters per second. That's the speed of its punch, not its swimming.

At number three, the glass frog. While it's sleeping, it hides eighty-nine percent of its red blood cells. Picture blood seemingly vanishing from view while the animal just rests there. That's its disappearing act.
But number one? Stranger. At number two, the wood frog. Its body can freeze, and its heartbeat stops. You might think that's the end. Then it thaws and survives. It's like nature pressing pause.

At number one, the ballooning spider. No wings, yet it can fly. Scientists even tested it in still air, removing wind from the equation. It still lifted off. So what was holding it up? The answer is something invisible: electric fields.

outro: And you thought superpowers were just fiction.
